field_product_items: • Clear clamshell packages of 10 oz. containing “thoughtfully handmade just for you Chicken Caesar Wrap with parmesan cheese lettuce, Caesar dressing" (Chicken Caesar Wrap with Parmesan Cheese Lettuce and Caesar Dressing, carefully made just for you) with best by dates of FEB 21, FEB 23, FEB 25, and lot codes LPK1WA046, LPK1WA048, LPK1WA050 printed on the label.
field_summary:
WASHINGTON, Feb. 23, 2025 – LPK1, a company in Renton, Wash., is recalling approximately 303 pounds of fully cooked Caesar chicken wraps due to labeling errors and undeclared allergens, the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) announced today. The Caesar dressing in the product, packaged individually, contains fish (anchovies), a known allergen, which is not declared on the product label.

The fully cooked Caesar chicken wraps were produced on Feb. 15, 2025, Feb. 17, 2025 and Feb. 19, 2025. The following products are subject to recall: [See Product Label Photos]:

  • Clear clamshell packages of 10 oz. containing “thoughtfully handmade just for you Chicken Caesar Wrap with parmesan cheese lettuce, Caesar dressing" (Chicken Caesar Wrap with Parmesan Cheese Lettuce and Caesar Dressing, carefully made just for you) with best by dates of FEB 21, FEB 23, FEB 25, and lot codes LPK1WA046, LPK1WA048, LPK1WA050 printed on the label.

The products subject to recall bear establishment number “P2276” inside the USDA mark of inspection. These items were distributed to vending machines in office buildings in Washington state.

The problem was discovered by the firm when it conducted a routine review of ingredient labels as part of its quality assurance process. The establishment subsequently notified FSIS that the product may contain fish (anchovies), which is not declared on the label.

No confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products have been received. Anyone concerned about an illness should contact a healthcare provider.

FSIS is concerned that part of the product may be in vending machines in office buildings. Consumers who purchased these products are urged not to consume them and offices are advised not to serve them. These products should be thrown away or returned to vending machine owners.

FSIS routinely conducts recall effectiveness checks to verify recalling firms notify their customers of the recall and that steps are taken to make certain the product is no longer available to consumers.

Media with questions about the recall can contact Kristin Elder, Public Relations Specialist, H+K Strategies, at kristin.elder@hkstrategies.com. Consumers with questions about the recall can contact Ryan Calbreath, Quality Assurance Manager, LPK1, at 925-457-6738 or ryan.calbreath@compass-usa.com.

Consumers with questions about food safety can call the USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 1-888-MPHotline (1-888-674-6854) or email MPHotline@usda.gov. Consumers wishing to report a problem with a meat, poultry or egg product can submit their concern using the online FSIS Recall Reporting System at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.
